title: Classic Traveller character record
$comment: Implements: The record matches the schema that describes it [JSON conventions] in The record.
description:
What ctchargen writes, as this build writes it. A description of the output, kept honest by the gate - not a promise to records already written. Nothing in it is hand-written, and nothing in it can be brought back by running the tool again: the dice are not seeded, so the record is the only way back to a character (ADR 0001). It carries every die of every roll and throw in order, and a draw that is not a throw appears as the choice it produced, so every number on a sheet can be checked against the page from the record alone.

Two of the optional benefit fields cannot appear together in any character this tool can generate. Book 1 p. 9 prints Travellers' Aid only in the Navy and Marines columns of Mustering Out Table 1, and the two starships only in the Scout and Merchant columns, and a character serves one service. So no valid record carries both travellersAid and ships. That is a fact about the rules rather than a gap in the fixtures, which is why character.complete.json shows the ships and not the membership.

The root object accepts a field it does not know; every object inside it does not. That is the narrower half of the v1.0.0 freeze, and it is deliberate (#76, #113). A later build may add a top-level section, and a reader holding this schema will load the record and render what it understands. A key added inside an existing object is still refused, and so is an event of a kind this build does not write, because those are the structures a sheet is rendered from and pinning them is what keeps this schema worth validating against.

record.$comment: Implements: A record from a later build validates and renders, which is what v1 promises [JSON conventions] in The record.
record.description: The shape of this record, not the build that wrote it and not the ruleset it reads. It is 1 until v1.0.0 and counts from there, not from every change: the record moves freely before the freeze, so a build that changes the shape before it leaves this alone and two pre-release shapes may both say 1. From v1.0.0 the shape is a public contract and a build that changes it says so here. A minimum rather than a fixed number, so that a record from a later build validates against a reader's copy of this schema instead of being refused before its contents are looked at; what this build writes is held to 1 by a test of its own.

name.description: Blank unless --name supplied one. Book 1 pp. 4-5 give naming as advice, not a table, so nothing generates one.

upp.description: The Universal Personality Profile (p. 8): the six characteristics as hexadecimal digits in rolled order. Derived from characteristics, and stored beside them so a reader need not re-derive it.

characteristics.$comment: Implements: A key a later build adds inside an existing object is still refused [JSON conventions] in The record.
characteristics.description: The six of p. 4, numeric. A value may reach 0 only through aging (E010); everything else floors at 1, and nothing exceeds 15.

age.description: Whole years, plus the months only a medical crisis recovery adds (pp. 7-8). Books 1-3 have no calendar and no birthdate rules, so the record carries an age and a count of terms, not a date.

terms.description: Terms of service, four years each (p. 5). Zero for a civilian. No upper bound: a 12 on the reenlistment throw recurs (E003).

how.description: P. 5. Declining is a complete record: an eighteen-year-old civilian (E001).

rank.description: An index into the service's own Table of Ranks (p. 10). Absent where the character holds none: rank 0 is not commissioned, and the Scouts and Other print no ranks at all.

rankName.description: What the Table of Ranks calls that rank in that service (p. 10). A name and not a title: the book keeps that word for nobility.

skills.description: Name and level, sorted by name. Where the rules demand a specific weapon, the name is that weapon's: p. 25's own list records Dagger-1, not Blade Combat.

travellersAid.description: Membership, achievable only once per character; a duplicate roll is wasted (p. 22).

weapons.description: Weapons received as benefits, which is narrower than the weapons held: expertise may be taken only in one received as a benefit (p. 22).

tons.description: The hull each is built on: Book 2 p. 18 for the Type S, p. 19 for the Type A.

paymentYears.description: Years of payments left on a Free Trader (pp. 22-23). A scout ship is held without title and carries none.

scoutShipsLost.description: Scout ships a duplicate roll lost. P. 23: "Only one scout ship may be acquired by a character, and throws resulting in additional ships are lost."

not.description: P. 9 prints Travellers' Aid only in the Navy and Marines columns of Mustering Out Table 1 and the two starships only in the Scout and Merchant columns, and a character serves one service. No record this tool can generate carries both.

annualRetirementPay.description: P. 21. Earned by leaving at the end of the fifth term or later, whatever caused it, and not available to the Scouts or Other.

departure.description: How the service ended. Absent for a civilian, who never joined one.

characteristic.description: The characteristic that reached zero, on a death by medical crisis (pp. 7-8, E008).

nobility.description: Assessed once, at the end of generation, against the final Social Standing, for every character including the dead - who are assessed but not asked (E011).

title.description: Book 3 p. 22, for Social Standing 11 through 15.

inputs.description: Everything the generation was given, so that a record says what made it.

service.description: Present when --service forced the enlistment attempt. It forces the attempt only: the throw is still made, and a failed throw still goes to the draft.

errata.description: Every recorded reading of rules/data/ERRATA.md that governed this record, in id order. A reading applied without appearing here is the one defect no gate catches.

ruleset.const: Classic Traveller, Books 1-3 (FFE reprint of the 1977 text)
ruleset.description: The text this record was generated under. Every page cite in its log is to these three books and nothing else.

policy.description: The version of the --auto policy that answered this record's choice points. Absent from a record the policy answered nothing in - one walked by hand - because naming a policy that decided none of it is a claim the record cannot support. It moves only when one of the policy's answers changes, which is what a referee reads to tell which answers made a record; ruleset names the rules and build names the writer, and neither moves for that reason.

build.description:
The build that wrote the record, from debug.ReadBuildInfo - the same source the version subcommand reports. Naming the build is what lets a referee say which code wrote the record he is reading or filing a report against.

The command fills it, and only the command: a record generated in-process by a test carries none, because a test binary's build info is not the build of a released tool and would make a golden differ by machine. So the goldens and the two examples beside this schema have no build, and a record written by ctchargen does.

events.description: The generation record: every step entered, throw made, choice answered and consequence, with monotonic sequence numbers. Walk it against Book 1 to audit any character.

service.description: The six of the Prior Service Table (p. 10), spelled as p. 5 lists them (E012).

dice.description: The dice as rolled, first die then second. The record logs the dice and not only their total, because that is what an auditor walks against the page.

target.description: The throw's target in the book's own notation (pp. 2-3). Required: a throw is the case that has something to meet, and a roll with nothing to meet is a rollEvent.

rollEvent.description: One roll with nothing to meet: the draft die, a skills table, a mustering out table, the months of recovery. It keeps the modifier, because the row the page is read at is the face plus the DM, and it carries no target and no outcome because there is nothing to succeed at.

dice.description: The dice as rolled. The record logs the dice and not only their total, because that is what an auditor walks against the page.

point.description: One per method of the Decider interface, which is what closes the set.

because.description: The throw or choice that caused this. Absent where the consequence follows from the procedure itself.
